facts.statement: The genus contains only one species, U. ceibalii, which is known solely from a single fossilized pubis bone.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, U. ceibalii, known only from a single fossilized pubis (a pelvic bone).

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PVL 3670-11 was discovered at Arroyo-Morterito in the Los Blanquitos Formation dating to the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: The holotype, PVL 3670-11, was found at Arroyo-Morterito in the Los Blanquitos Formation, dating to the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The type species Unquillosaurus ceibalii was described by Jaime Eduardo Powell in 1979.
facts.quote: The type species Unquillosaurus ceibalii was described by Jaime Eduardo Powell in 1979.

facts.statement: Powell originally assigned Unquillosaurus to the Carnosauria in 1979.
facts.quote: Powell (1979) assigned Unquillosaurus as a theropod of uncertain taxonomic placement, regarding it as a member of the Carnosauria.

facts.statement: In 2004, Novas and Agnolin concluded that Unquillosaurus belonged to Maniraptora or at least Maniraptoriformes based on opisthopubic pelvic anatomy.
facts.quote: In 2004, Novas and Agnolín concluded from the opisthopubic pelvic anatomy that Unquillosaurus was part of the Maniraptora or at least Maniraptoriformes

facts.statement: In 2006, Martínez and Novas suggested that Unquillosaurus likely belonged to the maniraptoran clade Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2006, Martínez and Novas stated that Unquillosaurus probably belonged to the maniraptoran clade Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: In 2012, Carrano and colleagues classified Unquillosaurus as a member of Carcharodontosauridae due to similarities with Giganotosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2012, however, Carrano and colleagues considered Unquillosaurus as a member of the Carcharodontosauridae, noting that the animal has many similarities to Giganotosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2024, researchers considering the taxonomy of Diuqin suggested Unquillosaurus might be a member of the Unenlagiinae.
facts.quote: In 2024, the describers of Diuqin considered this taxon to be a possible member of the Unenlagiinae.

facts.statement: Unquillosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 71 million years ago in the Campanian stage in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 y 71 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Unquillosaurus is estimated to have reached 3 meters in length, 1.40 meters in height, and weighed nearly 40 kilograms.
facts.quote: Unquillosaurus es un dromeosáurido que se estima que llegó a medir 3 metros de largo y 1,40 m de alto, pesando cerca de los 40 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Unquillosaurus ceibalii is the only known species of the extinct genus Unquillosaurus, a dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Unquillosaurus ceibalii es la única especie conocida del género extinto Unquillosaurus ("lagarto de Unquillo") de dinosaurio terópodo dromeosáurido

facts.statement: Initially, Unquillosaurus was thought to belong to a giant theropod 11 meters long.
facts.quote: En un principio se pensó que pertenecía a un terópodo gigante de 11 metros de largo.

facts.statement: In 2012, Carrano et al. reclassified the animal into Carnosauria, specifically Carcharodontosauria, suggesting the original interpretation was likely correct.
facts.quote: Carrano et al. en 2012, colocó al animal nuevamente en Carnosauria, específicamente en Carcharodontosauria y señaló que la interpretación original probablemente era correcta

facts.statement: The time range for Unquillosaurus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Unquillosaurus as Carcharodontosauridae.
